subject: surgery
title: Biliary tract pathology: choledocholithiasis, cholangiocarcinoma, and bile duct injury repair

steps.tx: Choledocholithiasis refers to the presence of **calculi** within the common bile duct, arising secondarily from the gallbladder or primarily in the bile ducts during stasis. Patients present with biliary colic, fluctuating obstructive jaundice, and elevated alkaline phosphatase and conjugated bilirubin. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (**ERCP**) with sphincterotomy and stone extraction is the first-line therapeutic modality, followed by interval laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
steps.say: Choledocholithiasis presents with biliary colic, obstructive jaundice, and elevated conjugated bilirubin. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with sphincterotomy and stone clearance is first line, followed by laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

nodes.label: Gallstones migrate into common bile duct

Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy during same admission

steps.tx: Acute **cholangitis** is a life-threatening infection of the biliary tree resulting from bacterial superinfection proximal to biliary obstruction. Charcot triad characterizes classic cholangitis: fever, right upper quadrant pain, and jaundice. Progression to Reynolds pentad adds septic shock and altered mental status, indicating suppurative ascending infection requiring emergency biliary decompression via ERCP or percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage (**PTBD**) within hours of admission.
steps.say: Acute cholangitis results from biliary obstruction combined with bacterial infection. Charcot triad includes fever, right upper quadrant pain, and jaundice. Reynolds pentad adds shock and confusion. Immediate emergent biliary decompression is life-saving.

steps.tx: Iatrogenic bile **duct** injury during laparoscopic cholecystectomy is categorized using the Strasberg classification. The classic major injury (Strasberg type E) results from misidentifying the common bile duct as the cystic duct, clipping and dividing it. Type E injuries are subdivided based on distance from the hepatic bifurcation (Bismuth levels E1 through E5). Definitive repair mandates tension-free, end-to-side Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy performed by an experienced hepatobiliary surgeon.
steps.say: Bile duct injury during cholecystectomy is classified by the Strasberg system. Complete transection of the common bile duct represents a type E injury. Definitive repair requires an experienced hepatobiliary team performing a Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy.

rows: Cystic duct leak or small duct of Luschka leak

Occlusion or transection of aberrant right hepatic duct

Complete circumferential transection / occlusion of CBD

steps.tx: Cholangiocarcinoma is classified anatomically into intrahepatic, perihilar (**Klatskin** tumors), and distal subtypes. Perihilar tumors account for 60 percent of cases and are categorized by the Bismuth-Corlette classification. Type I tumors involve the common hepatic duct distal to bifurcation; Type II involves the bifurcation; Type III involves the bifurcation extending into the right (IIIa) or left (IIIb) hepatic duct; Type IV involves bilateral secondary hepatic ducts. Resection requires en bloc hepatectomy with biliary reconstruction.
steps.say: Perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, or Klatskin tumor, is staged by the Bismuth-Corlette classification. Type one is below the confluence, type two involves the confluence, type three extends into unilateral branches, and type four involves bilateral ducts.
